summary: Verified the OpenAI Realtime beta->GA migration fix on the Twilio Media Streams bridge. Live wss://.../api/voice/media simulation: sent Twilio-style start + 20 mu-law silence frames, received 20 inbound 'media' frames with time-to-first-audio ~0.79s. No beta_api_shape_disabled error in the current backend process (the single occurrence in backend.err.log at line 1383 predates the last supervisor restart at line 1460). Readiness, mock-agent simulate regression (5 turns -> submit tool, budget per turn, transcript>=5, linked order_id), REST vertical slice with idempotent submit, and verify-caller guards (invalid_phone + confirmation_required) all pass. Full pytest suite 84/84 in 8.3s.
critical_code_review_comments: openai_realtime.py GA shape looks correct: session.type='realtime', nested audio.input/output with audio/pcmu, output_modalities=['audio'], no OpenAI-Beta header, response.output_audio.delta event handled.
MediaOrchestrator successfully bridges mu-law 8k in both directions; TTFA ~0.79s for silence input is healthy.
verify-caller confirm=true still places a real billable call by design; document/guard in UI to avoid accidents.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_media_ws.py hits real wss endpoint and opens a small-cost OpenAI Realtime session per run (intended for regression). Run standalone: `python /app/backend/tests/test_media_ws.py`. On PASS you should see '>=1 inbound media frames'. If it regresses to 0, first check /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log for 'beta_api_shape_disabled' or 4xx close codes from OpenAI. Full pytest suite = 84 tests, ~8s. Do NOT POST confirm=true to /api/voice/verify-caller (real call).
